Use it only as low-confidence context or for sensitivity analysis, never as the sole basis for a species model.
Keep the secondary multi-species table labelled as secondary throughout.

value.quote: 2. Keep biological quantities compatible. Separate routes (oral gavage, intraperitoneal, IV), total versus unbound drug, serum versus plasma versus free brain dialysate, and bioassay versus chromatographic results. Keep single-dose, day-2, repeat-dose and post-treatment samples apart; exposure is nonlinear and falls with repeated dosing in mice and rats, so parameters from one dose or day do not transfer to another. Keep neutropenic, non-neutropenic, infected, meningitis, grapefruit-juice and co-medicated animals apart. Every conversion requires a recorded justification.

value.quote: 3. Predict human PK. Translate supported animal models using body size, protein binding, metabolic clearance and justified physiological relationships, accounting for nonlinearity and autoinduction before scaling. Compare approaches with and without each species rather than assuming more species is better. Predict human concentration-time profiles, AUC, Cmax and Cmin with uncertainty under specified IV and oral regimens, including loading doses, and freeze them before opening human outcomes.
